changes: Druids in Cat or Bear Form now gain 1 attack power per point of Strength and Agility; Agility consumables are usable in feral forms.
Swipe no longer costs mana and is only usable in Bear or Cat Form.
Dungeon companions now have traits: group buffs that fit your resource, and Druids or Warlocks can rescue a wipe once per run with Rebirth or Soulstone.
New dungeons: Razorfen Kraul (Lv 29–35) and Scarlet Monastery (Lv 34–42), each with five bosses, loot and their own scenery.
Shadowfang Keep and Blackfathom Deeps now have their own dungeon scenery.
The return trip from a dungeon can no longer be cancelled.
The death penalty badge now sits on the player portrait.
Fixed missing talent tree backgrounds.
Bear Form and Cat Form can no longer be learned together
Right-click a talent to remove a point again, as long as no other talent depends on it
New "Improved" talent in tier 4 of every tree that strengthens the ability talent of tier 2 (e.g. Improved Cat Form, Improved Evocation)
Faerie Fire (Bear/Cat) now requires Improved Maul/Improved Claw; talents that depend on each other are connected by arrows
Characters whose talents break the new rules get their talent points for that class refunded
The world map is more compact and looks more like a map; finished zones get a green check.
Zones far below your level no longer give discovery XP or zone objectives – only their profession drops remain. They are shown as small faded labels.
Death penalty is now shown as a small circle badge (- 5%) on the XP bar instead of a separate text line.
Talent trees always show 7 tiers with a vertical tier bar showing the points needed for the next tier
Reworked talent tooltips: requirements such as level, current and next rank effect, click hints
Reset Talents button centered and styled like the menu buttons
The zone tooltip sums up the travel route in one line; the reduced XP hint is only shown in the tooltip.
Added Shadowfang Keep dungeon (levels 22–27, 5 bosses, Archmage Arugal as final boss)
Added Blackfathom Deeps dungeon (levels 26–32, 5 bosses, Aku'mai as final boss)
Added loot for Shadowfang Keep and Blackfathom Deeps — including Trinket and Chest items not covered by earlier dungeons
Spells with fixed values now gain a new rank every 10 levels and at level 60. You are notified about new ranks of equipped spells.
The Ability Loadout now lets you set auto-cast conditions for each spell, based on your resource or health in percent. Tooltips and slots show the active conditions.
You can now wear two rings and two trinkets at the same time. A second copy of a ring or trinket is no longer sold automatically.
The crafting queue now shows your free inventory slots and pauses while the inventory has no room for the next result.
New crafting queue option for enchanters: crafted uncommon gear is disenchanted right after crafting.
Professions and their trainers now glow when new training or a better bonus is available.
Every race now has two passive racial traits, such as more damage, attack speed or a cheaper merchant. They are shown during character creation and in the Inventory.
Raised the level cap from 10 to 15.
Dungeon bosses now make an entrance: the screen darkens, the boss speaks a line, and the fight starts after a few seconds.
Attacks from dungeon enemies and especially bosses now look much heavier.
The XP lost on death drops by 1 percentage point for each character of yours at the next ten-level mark (for example level 20+ for levels 10–19). A tooltip below the XP bar shows your current loss.
Money is now shared by all your characters. The money your characters already have is added together.
Tailoring, Leatherworking and Blacksmithing can now craft expensive blue hands and wrists for every class (level 10, skill 25).
The crafting window now has one Create button that uses the amount field, which starts at 1 and resets when you pick another recipe.
Flight points now unlock for your whole account, and reaching a dungeon unlocks its flight point too. Everything your characters have already visited stays unlocked.
Wailing Caverns and The Deadmines now have their own animated scenery.
Changing the race of an existing character now starts a 24-hour cooldown for that character.
You can jump again as soon as the previous jump has finished.
Enemy names no longer repeat the level, and rare and dungeon enemies show it only on their portrait.
Fixed health, mana, XP and meter bars jumping back during combat on Linux.

Added two dungeons for both factions: Wailing Caverns (level 17-24) and The Deadmines (level 18-23). Each has five bosses with trash groups in front of them. They appear on the zone map but stay locked until the level cap rises above the current limit.

Build your dungeon group by dragging your character and NPCs into one tank, one healer and three damage slots. Companions cast real spells, share one health bar with you and appear in the damage and healing meters.
Each character can start 3 dungeon runs per 12 hours. The third death ends a run, and after every run your character travels back to the previous zone at double speed.
Every dungeon boss drops one item usable by your class. Each dungeon has 3 class sets of 5 pieces with 2, 3 and 5 piece bonuses, shown in the item tooltip.
Dungeon weapons can be limited to several classes, and tooltips list them.
Added achievements for completing each dungeon and for wearing a full dungeon set.
Tooltips no longer stay on screen while dragging an item or character.
Fixed combat slowing down the longer the game runs on Linux.
Enemies now drop more cloth at once: humanoids 2–4, rare enemies 4–6 and all others 1–3.
Added a Healing Meter next to the Damage Meter. Log and Reset cover both.

Mounts must now be learned: a riding trainer of your race appears in your Inventory from level 40 (60% speed, 100 gold) and level 60 (100% speed, 1000 gold), per character. Characters already past these levels need to train too.
Mounts have their own slot in the character window. Click it to switch mounts. Mounts follow your race, and class mounts were removed.
Item tooltips and comparisons now show special equip effects.
First Aid can now craft stimpaks: used automatically right after resurrecting, they raise your Spirit for a short time.
Tailoring can now craft cloaks for every class.
Alchemy can now craft Alchemist's Stones, trinkets that make healing and mana potions of their tier restore 30% more. Enchanting can craft the Charm of Keen Insight (+1% Critical Strike chance).
Rare and epic profession bonuses now drop less often: 0.5% and 0.25% per kill instead of 1%.
The crafting queue shows the total time left and can return you to combat when it runs empty (unlocks at level 15).
Recipe lists show how many of an item are in your bags, the class filter keeps recipes for all classes, and the profession quick bar shows which characters work passively.
Combat zones are now grouped by level range.
Zones show only what is still open: finished objectives and found drops disappear. A popup appears once you complete a zone.
Press Space on the Idle Fighter page to jump, with achievements for jumping.
Added achievements for collecting and equipping profession bonuses.
The Changelog page now marks builds you haven't seen yet.
Every class now learns three new spec-themed abilities between levels 11 and 15.
Added a third talent row from level 20 with one talent per tree that improves these abilities.

Hunter: Mongoose Bite has a shorter cooldown, deals more damage and empowers your next Raptor Strike by 45%. Several talents were strengthened, and the Raptor Strike and Serpent Sting talents now add damage.
Mage: reduced Arcane damage. Arcane Missiles, Evocation, Arcane Instability and Improved Arcane Missiles are weaker.
Druid: Bear Form and Cat Form talents are now available from level 12.
Warrior: the Execute cooldown talent now reduces the cooldown by 20 seconds per rank.
Default loadouts now always keep your main no-cooldown attack, and ability tooltips describe debuffs, retaliation damage and pet bonuses.
The combat meter now also counts healing from lifesteal, Smite, Critical Heal and potions.
Added profession bonuses: rare drops from combat zones that improve skill-up chance, speed or double-item chance. Equip them account-wide in 3 slots per profession.
Crafting and disenchanting now run through one account-wide crafting queue. It survives character switches, is saved, and runs while the professions menu is open.
Blacksmithing recipes no longer need stone. Each reagent amount is 1 higher instead.
Combat zones now show which profession bonuses drop there and which ones you have found.
The Changelog page now groups changes by category.
Switching characters in the profession windows no longer changes your played character once you leave them.
The Ability Loadout now lists talent abilities you haven't learned yet under Coming Up, including which talent unlocks them and what it requires.
New crafting materials now go to bags 1 and 3 first, consumables to bags 2 and 4. Existing stacks are always topped up before a new slot is used.
Added craftable level 10 gear (hands, belt, feet) for Tailoring, Leatherworking and Blacksmithing.
Crafting and disenchanting skill-up chance now rises by 0.2% per 10 levels across all your characters.
The profession trainer window now keeps a fixed size, so the Train button no longer moves when you select a recipe.
The sidebar now shows a travel countdown while you are on other pages. Click it to return to the travel scene.
The game now reopens the page you were on when you last closed it.
Added hotkeys: B or C opens the Inventory, F the Idle Fighter, K Professions and N Talents.
Added a Changelog page to the menu that shows what changed in each build.
From level 10, each death costs 5% of your current XP. You never lose a level.
Current health and mana, rage or energy are now saved and restored on load.
The new ability popup in Idle Fighter now stays until you dismiss it. The × closes it without equipping the ability.
Fixed misplaced and see-through tooltips on upcoming abilities in the Ability Loadout.
Elixirs and buff food now last 3 minutes instead of 1.
Fixed dragging characters into zone slots on Linux.
Consumables can be toggled on the combat bar with a right-click.
Health and mana potions now have separate cooldowns.
Gathering professions: passive runs take 90 seconds instead of 120, and skill-ups only come from passive gathering.
Professions are now unlocked in the menu for the whole account.
Updates are now checked every minute while playing, and the game saves before restarting.
Items can be moved between inventory slots and bags with drag & drop.
Travel now continues while you are on other pages.
